ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended, especially Articles 19, 20, 258 and 260); Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Information (Act No. 11785, as amended, the principal AML/CFT statute and the legal basis of the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit or KFIU); Proceeds of Crime Act; Corporate Tax Act (Act No. 16039, as amended, Article 6 on domestic corporation place of effective management); Local Tax Act; Real Name Financial Transactions Act; the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961 Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents as ratified by the Republic of Korea and implemented through Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille procedures.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Registered Corporation Facts (Certificate of Incorporation for a Yuhan Hoesa issuing from the Korean Supreme Court registry system)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry Office having jurisdiction over the principal business office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: obtain the registry certificate, have any ancillary signature notarized by a Korean licensed notary when required by the receiving party, then submit to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille Division in the Republic of Korea for a single Apostille Certificate. Consular Legalization path for non-Hague states: notarize, authenticate before the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Authentication Division, then legalize before the competent Republic of Korea consulate in the destination jurisdiction. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Business Registration Certificate (tax good standing evidence from the National Tax Service)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service district tax office at the registered business place of business
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague path: issue from the Korean National Tax Service, notarize signatures if required, and obtain a Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille Certificate. Non-Hague path: notarize, complete Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, and obtain consular legalization from the Korean consulate. Never combine Apostille with consular legalization for the same destination.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing Korean counsel and authorized signatories for pre-incorporation and bank/payment-processing tasks
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa managing members assembled in a properly recorded initial meeting, with notarized signatures before a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Convention states: execute and notarize in Korea, then obtain a Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille Certificate. For non-member states: execute and notarize, obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then submit to the relevant Republic of Korea consulate for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative routes, not sequential steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (the charter instrument of the Yuhan Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public, with a certified copy or registration excerpt issued by the District Court Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague path: notarized Korean original or certified registry copy, then apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Korea. Consular path for non-Hague jurisdictions: notarized document, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then legalized by the competent Korean consulate. The two legalization paths are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Payment Channel Compliance Letter for Stripe, PayPal, and Korean settlement accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A Korean commercial bank licensed by the Financial Services Commission and operating a compliant KFIU AML program
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: bank signs the reference, bank officer signature is notarized or confirmed by legal counsel, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs issues an Apostille. Consular path: after notarization and Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, destination-specific consular legalization is obtained. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate Seal Registration Certificate and Authorized Signatory Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean District Court Registry Office where the corporate seal and registered representative's personal seal are recorded
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague path: registry-issued certificate is apostilled directly through the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille Division. Non-Hague path: certificate is notarized, authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Authentication Division, and then consular legalized by the Korean consulate of the destination. Parallel and exclusive; no sequential application of both methods.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screening must cover all ultimate beneficial owners, founding managers, directors, authorized signatories, and nominees against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit designated list, Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions, the UN Security Council consolidated list, the OFAC SDN list, EU restrictive measures, and Korean domestic sanctions lists. Conduct risk-based enhanced due diligence on PEPs, family members, close associates, former PEPs who left public office within the prior twelve months, and any entity owned or controlled by sanctioned persons. Identity verification must include government-issued photo ID, passport, corporate registration data, corporate seal certificate, and bank confirmation. Transaction behavior, payment processor volume, crowdfunding patterns, and cross-border payment counterparties must be reviewed for evasion red flags. All screening results and underlying records must be retained for at least five years, and suspicious transactions reported to KFIU under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Information.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-REG) and the District Court Commercial Registry serving the intended principal office, with formal name clearance checked at the moment of incorporation filing; if a name reservation is separately requested by the filing bank, it is handled through the Korean Registry system.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean company names must be written entirely in the Korean alphabet and must include the statutory entity suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' for a limited liability company; English names may be registered only as a trade alias for payment and export purposes, not as the controlling registry name. Foreign-language trade names must be transliterated phonetically into Korean script. The four-tier naming convention applied by the registry is: first, the statutory entity suffix; second, the distinctive Korean trade name; third, the optional industry-descriptive segment such as tabletop game manufacturing or dice casting; and fourth, the optional English romanized alias. The registry rejects names identical, deceptively similar, or phonetically identical to any existing registered company in the same registry district; no misleading reference to a different corporate form such as 'Jusik Hoesa' is permitted for a Yuhan Hoesa.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the District Court Registrar rejects the proposed Yuhan Hoesa trade name, counsel must file a written objection with the registrar under the Commercial Registration Act and the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act promptly after receiving the written rejection, ordinarily within one week. The objection must state why the name is not identical or deceptively similar, attach prior trademark or domain searches, and include written consent or coexistence evidence when available. If the registrar maintains the refusal, an appeal may be filed with the competent District Court civil panel, and thereafter an administrative review can be pursued in connection with registry instructions. Any ministerial authorization for a prohibited sensitive token must be secured before the final filing, and the appeal should expressly demonstrate that the name will not mislead the public regarding corporate form, scale, or government affiliation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The Korean registry will accept a serviced office address for corporate registration, but a mail-only virtual office is not sufficient for full commercial substance in the tabletop gaming dice manufacturing industry. Korean tax authorities and commercial banks, and in practice Stripe, PayPal, and local acquiring banks, require a verifiable physical operating location or demonstrable production and fulfillment premises. A pure virtual office creates a material risk that the National Tax Service will reject business registration amendments, that a bank will refuse account opening under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act, and that payment processors will hold funds pending address verification. The recommended structure is a physical workshop or fulfillment space registered as the business establishment, with a commercial correspondence service used in addition, not instead, of that physical place.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced inspection risk for a compliant Yuhan Hoesa with ISIC 3240 operations is low but not negligible. The National Tax Service and local municipal tax authorities may conduct an on-site inspection when VAT refund claims exceed expected output, when crowdfunding or payment processor settlements are disproportionate to reported revenue, when a home office is used for manufacturing, or when non-resident ownership and management concentration are present. Estimated annual inspection probability is approximately five percent for a cleanly structured LLC with a physical workshop and approximately eight to twelve percent if the company operates from a home or virtual office. The company should keep ready for inspection: original lease and utility statements, board minutes, product inventory, dice molds and production tools, shipping and courier logs, raw material purchase invoices, bank settlement reports, payment processor transaction summaries, and a visible sign or stable reception function at the registered address.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Korean local registration tax for incorporating a Yuhan Hoesa with ordinary nominal paid-in capital of KRW 10,000,000, including local education surtax
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Mayor, County Administrator, or Local District Office levying the Local Tax Act registration tax
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Local Tax Act statutory tariff of 0.4% of capital plus 20% local education surcharge.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: District Court commercial registration filing fee for the initial incorporation registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court Registry Office through the relevant District Court Commercial Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Korean Commercial Registration Fee scale for Yuhan Hoesa registration, approximately KRW 45,000 plus electronic filing and postage service charges.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Articles of Association, founding member resolutions, certified signature pages, and power of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean notary public engaged by organizing counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Korean Notary Fee Act notarial tariff, with prevailing market benchmark of KRW 150,000 to KRW 300,000 depending on document count.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation name clearance, i-REG search, trademark search, and corporate due diligence by Korean special counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Korean attorney or licensed foreign legal consultant office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Seoul market benchmark for Stage 1 corporate due diligence and name clearance in the KR Yuhan Hoesa pipeline.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO, PEP, OFAC, UN, Korean KFIU, and EU sanctions screening plus AML/CFT record bundle preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean AML/CFT compliance provider or law firm subscription to KFIU-compatible screening databases
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market compliance benchmark for multi-jurisdictional beneficial ownership and sanctions screening, including adverse media review.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization fees for the mandatory documentary bundle of six instruments
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea Apostille and Authentication Divisions plus the applicable Korean consulate for non-Hague states
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: MOFA official fee per Apostille or authentication certificate plus destination consular legalization fee and courier/handling expenses.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified copies of registered corporation facts, seal registration certificate, and original registry-issued incorporation evidence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: District Court Registry Office of the Republic of Korea
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Supreme Court registry certificate fee scale.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: National Tax Service business registration certificate and tax clearance certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official government fee is charged for issuance of the business registration certificate and tax clearance; this item is zero under Korean law.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as most recently amended), Book IV (Company), Chapter VII (Limited Liability Company), Articles 287-1 et seq.; together with the Commercial Registration Act (Sang-eop Deunggi-beop) and the Framework Act on Commercial Registration
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Office of the Commercial Registration Division of the District Court in whose jurisdiction the registered head office is situated (in Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Commercial Registration Division), with e-filing through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa Seollip Deunggi) together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act or the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The subscribed contribution amounts are stated in the Articles of Incorporation and must be deposited into a Korean bank provisional deposit account before registration; the bank issues a capital contribution verification certificate presented to the court. The deposit is blocked only until the registration is completed, after which the funds become freely available for corporate use. Court registration tax and local education tax are assessed on the actual contributed capital, generally at 0.4 percent and 0.2 percent respectively, plus any minimum court stamp fees.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF MANAGERS OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) ORGANIZED UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA, DATED [DATE]. The Board of Managers, being the persons who have consented to act as the inaugural managing body of the corporation executing the instrument identified under task ISIC_3240_10_TABLETOP_ROLEPLAY_POLYHEDRAL_DICE, hereby adopts the following resolutions, each by unanimous written consent and effective upon the state registration of the company. 1. Registered Office: The registered office shall be fixed at [address, Si/Gun/Gu, South Korea], and the corporate seal, statutory records, and legal notice book shall be maintained there. The managers are authorized to execute the office lease and file the registered office adoption notice with the competent court registry. 2. Capital Subscription and Issuance: The total contributed capital is Korean Won [amount], divided into [number] non-par-value contributions of [amount] each. Each subscribing member shall remit the full amount to a provisional capital deposit account at [Bank] before registration, and the bank certificate of contribution shall be delivered to the registration court. Contributions carry the legal rights and restrictions of a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act. 3. Banking Authorization: The Board designates [Bank], [branch], as principal depository. [Name], Chief Managing Member, and [Name], second authorized manager, are jointly authorized to open and operate disbursement accounts and payment service provider accounts, including Kickstarter Stripe and PayPal business accounts, and to sign checks, wire instructions, and settlement agreements. Transactions above USD [amount] require joint signature. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments: [Name] is appointed first Chief Managing Member and legal representative of the company with authority to execute industrial permits, leases, statutory filings, and commercial contracts. [Name] is appointed second managing member and compliance officer for occupational safety, environmental, and product-safety matters. [Name] is appointed internal auditor and monitor for accounting controls. All officers assume office upon filing of their consents with the court and shall serve until removed or replaced by a members resolution. 5. Authorizations and Continuing Effect: The Board authorizes the legal representatives to complete notarization, court registration, tax registration, factory establishment reporting, environmental assessment, fire safety inspections, and all ancillary filings. The Board further authorizes the legal representatives to make non-substantive amendments requested by the court and to take all lawful actions necessary to commence the epoxy resin dice manufacturing business. This resolution is irrevocable and shall be certified in the formation dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name clearance, notarization of articles, and registered office address verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public under the Notary Act of Korea and the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS); address verification with the local Si/Gun/Gu administrative office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on IROS for the proposed company name Yuhan Hoesa and its romanized form YUHANGHOESA. If the name is available and not misleading, prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation for a limited liability company. The articles must state the company name, business object covering ISIC 3240 manufacture of tabletop and role-playing polyhedral dice, resin casting, packaging, wholesale and retail, the registered office address, contributed capital, number of contributions, contribution method, managers powers, and the term of the company, if any. Each founder or authorized agent must appear personally before a Korean notary, sign the articles, and obtain an authenticated deed. Simultaneously, collect a lease contract or owner consent letter for the registered office address and ensure the premises are zoned for manufacturing or permitted small-scale production.
required_dossiers: Name search result printout from IROS
Notarized Articles of Incorporation in Korean (two originals)
Passport or Alien Registration Certificate of each founder and manager
Registered office address proof (lease contract or owner consent)
Lessor consent to use the office as corporate seat
Power of attorney for a local filing agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity or prohibited expressions, submit a new name or a written explanation against the rejection with the court registry. If the notary requires corrections, convene a fresh meeting of the founders and re-execute the articles. No authenticated change is required for a purely typographical correction of romanization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital subscription escrow deposit and bank capital verification certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Services Commission-licensed Korean deposit-taking bank, for example Kookmin Bank, Hana Bank, or Shinhan Bank, at a physical branch or through official corporate onboarding channels
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional capital deposit account in the name of the company in formation. Each subscribing member must wire or deposit the full contribution amount into this account before court registration. The bank will collect the notarized articles, subscriber list, beneficial ownership information, and source-of-funds documentation. The bank must also verify the identity of foreign subscribers and issue a capital contribution verification certificate, also called a deposit certificate, showing the company name, amount, date, and depositor. For non-cash contributions such as resin production equipment, prepare a court-appointed appraiser report and a certificate of delivery of the in-kind property to the companys registered office.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Subscriber or member list with contribution amounts
Passport or Alien Registration Certificate of each contributing person
Bank anti-money laundering source-of-funds declaration
Bank beneficial ownership form
Power of attorney for bank account opening, if executed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional anti-money laundering evidence, submit tax returns, crypto-to-fiat conversion statements, sales platform reports, and a sworn declaration of fund origin. If the provisional account is suspended for name mismatch, apply to the court deposit office for a provisional deposit and use the court receipt as the capital verification certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court filing of establishment registration and payment of registration tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the competent District Court; online filing through Supreme Court of Korea IROS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the prescribed application for registration of establishment of the Yuhan Hoesa with the commercial registration division. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital contribution deposit certificate, written consent of each appointed manager, member list, proof of the registered office, and power of attorney. Pay court registration tax and local education tax through IROS or the court treasury counter based on the actual contribution amount. The court examiner will review substantive legality, name compliance, and completeness. Upon approval, the company is registered and the court issues a certificate of registered matters, which is conclusive proof of legal personality. There is no minimum capital condition for the court to accept the filing.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of establishment of Yuhan Hoesa
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital contribution deposit certificate or in-kind appraiser report
Written consent of each manager to assume office
Certificate of factual registered office (lease or owner consent)
Receipt of payment of registration tax and local education tax
Power of attorney and legal counsel identification, if represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction or supplementation order, file the requested documentation within the prescribed statutory period, typically 14 days. If the examiner refuses registration, submit a corrected application or an administrative brief in Korean through local counsel. If the statutory period is missed, reinstate by filing a new application with a fresh registration tax receipt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration, corporate bank account activation, and post-incorporation statutory reports
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service Hometax portal and local district tax office; Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) for foreign investment reports; Financial Services Commission for foreign exchange bank reports
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days after the court registration, file the business registration certificate application with Hometax. Use the corporate registration certificate, articles, manager identification, lease contract, and factory address to register as a manufacturing business under ISIC 3240. Request corporate electronic tax invoices and then activate the corporate operating bank account by presenting the certificate of registered matters, business registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, the board resolution, and signature cards. Upon activation, release the provisional capital deposit. Register the company seal with the competent registry and, if any subscriber is a non-resident, file the foreign-investment report with KOTRA or a reporting bank when the investment is KRW 100 million or above, or earlier if benefits are claimed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registered matters from the court
Corporate seal certificate and company seal registration card
Business registration application filed through Hometax
Articles of Incorporation and board resolution
Identity documents of the manager and authorized signatories
Lease contract and factory address proof
Foreign investment report, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service rejects the business classification because the premises appear non-operational, submit photographs, floor plans, equipment invoices, and a utility contract showing active use. If the foreign investment report is rejected, apply to KOTRA for ex-post amendment or re-file at the appropriate bank with a certified translation of the corporate registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial factory establishment report, environmental screening, fire safety, and civil-defense operating permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Si/Gun/Gu municipal licensing office; National Fire Agency and local fire station; Ministry of Employment and Labor regional office; local environmental agency under the Ministry of Environment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing production, file the Factory Establishment Report under the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act. The report must describe the process of mixing epoxy resin, casting liquid-core polyhedral dice, trimming sharp edges, polishing, quality control, and packaging. Include the site plan, structural drawings, equipment list, chemical inventory, ventilation system, waste storage area, and safety management plan. If wastewater will be generated from cleaning or cooling, file the wastewater dischargeer report under the Water Environment Conservation Act. If hazardous chemicals are stored or used above thresholds, register as a hazardous chemical business under the Chemicals Control Act. Submit the fire safety plan to the local fire station and obtain a fire and civil defense inspection certificate. Register compliance with the Occupational Safety and Health Act by appointing a safety manager, preparing material safety data sheets, and submitting a workplace accident prevention plan.
required_dossiers: Factory establishment report form
Certificate of registered matters and business registration certificate
Site and floor plan stamped by a certified architect
Chemical inventory and safety data sheets under the Korea MSDS system
Wastewater and waste generation report, if applicable
Fire safety and civil defense permit application
Occupational safety and health management plan and employee industrial insurance receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the factory report is rejected, submit a correction plan limiting capacity, adding ventilation, or installing a small wastewater treatment unit. If environmental review is triggered, prepare a small-scale environmental impact review under the Ministry of Environment. If fire safety is non-compliant, install the required extinguishers, exits, grounding, and flammable liquid storage cabinet, then apply for re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Si/Gun/Gu municipal government as the single-window licensing office, in coordination with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, the Ministry of SMEs and Startups, the National Fire Agency, the Ministry of Employment and Labor, and the Ministry of Environment
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Establishment Report Certificate and Manufacturing Business License under the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act; Wastewater Discharger Report under the Water Environment Conservation Act; Hazardous Chemical Operator Registration under the Chemicals Control Act if applicable; Civil Defense Fire Safety Inspection Certificate; Workplace Safety and Health Compliance Certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, Environmental Impact Assessment Bureau, and the local river basin environmental office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from Full Environmental Impact Assessment for a micro-scale epoxy resin dice casting studio with gross floor area below 10,000 square meters and project site area below 25,000 square meters. A Prior Environmental Review or Small-Scale Environmental Impact Consultation may be required if the site is located in an environmentally protected area, if wastewater discharge exceeds the local sewerage capacity, or if the floor area exceeds the thresholds specified in the enforcement decree.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from cleaning and cooling must meet Korea Water Environment Conservation Act effluent standards, including BOD not exceeding 30 mg/L, COD not exceeding 40 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L, total nitrogen not exceeding 60 mg/L, and total phosphorus not exceeding 8 mg/L if the water is treated in a private facility; domestic sewage must be discharged to the public sewer. Air emissions from epoxy resin mixing and curing stations must be controlled by local exhaust ventilation with a combined VOC capture and abatement efficiency of at least 90 percent, and workplace exposure to bisphenol A diglycidyl ether must not exceed 0.1 mg/m3. Hazardous waste such as cured resin scrap, contaminated containers, and polishing dust must be transported and treated only by a licensed waste handler and manifested under the Waste Management Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the municipal fire station is mandatory, including fire extinguishers, fire exits, flame-retardant storage cabinets for liquid resin and hardeners, static-electricity grounding, and a civil defense emergency evacuation plan. A structural load inspection by a registered architect is required for the casting, curing, and storage areas. The Ministry of Employment and Labor must accept the workplace safety management plan, safety officer appointment, material safety data sheets, chemical risk assessment, and training records for all workers handling sharp-edge dice and epoxy resins.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating through the HomeTax electronic tax portal; Korea Customs Service (KCS) handles export declaration processing through the UNI-PASS national customs portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Under the Korean VAT Act and Framework Act on National Taxes, a foreign non-resident entity carrying on any VAT-taxable business in Korea must file an application for Business Operator Registration with the district tax office having jurisdiction over its domestic place of business, or with the Seoul Central District Tax Office if there is no fixed domestic place of business. The NTS then assigns a 10-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as the unified TIN and VAT ID. The submission package for a foreign entity must include: (1) the prescribed business registration application submitted through HomeTax or in person; (2) a certified copy of the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation or registration, plus articles of association or equivalent constitutive documents, notarized and apostilled where required; (3) a board resolution or power of attorney appointing a tax agent in Korea, and, where the entity has no domestic business office, an express designation of a domestic tax representative; (4) evidence of the domestic place of business such as a lease agreement or ownership deed when applicable; (5) for digital commerce, evidence of the foreign legal representative appointment and the consent for service of process under Korean tax law; and (6) supporting documents showing the actual commencement date of the business. Registration must be completed before starting the Korean taxable activity, and failure or delay in registration may expose the entity to unregistered-business additional tax penalties. The same 10-digit registration number is used for VAT and for KCS exporter registration, enabling the applicant to file export declarations in UNI-PASS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not provide a check-the-box election or a flow-through entity election for a Yuhan Hoesa; it is treated as a domestic corporation under the Korean Corporate Tax Act and is taxed at entity level on worldwide income. Shareholders are separately taxed on dividend distributions. No hybrid mismatch election is available under the Korean tax law framework, although Korea applies anti-hybrid rules consistent with the OECD BEPS recommendations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold: any entrepreneur supplying goods or services in Korea in the course of business must register for VAT from the first taxable supply. A simplified taxable person regime exists for small business operators with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80,000,000, but this is a special accounting and relief regime and does not exempt the entity from registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses are obliged to issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax Electronic Tax Invoice System, in accordance with Article 32 of the VAT Act, and to transmit the issuance data to the NTS through the HomeTax API or an accredited special service provider. There is no physical fiscal stamp or real-time transaction-level clearance; instead, NTS conducts system-based validation, cross-matching of electronic tax invoice data against VAT returns, and anti-fraud reconciliation. Late submission or non-transmission of electronic tax invoice data triggers electronic tax invoice penalties, and issuance of false electronic tax invoices is subject to criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating is available under the VAT Act when goods are actually exported from Korea to a foreign country, evidenced by a customs export declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service and by credible transport documents showing the goods left the Korean customs territory. Services, including offshore digital services, may also qualify for zero-rating where they are supplied to a non-resident or foreign corporation, are performed or consumed outside Korea, and the statutory supporting evidence is retained by the Korean exporter. For goods, the exporter must complete export within the legally permitted period and repatriate export proceeds in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. For services and digital supplies, the taxpayer must retain the contract with the foreign customer, proof of the customer's non-resident status, evidence that the service is consumed outside Korea, and bank or remittance records proving settlement in foreign currency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration certificate (Export Entry) issued through UNI-PASS
Original Bill of Lading for sea freight, Air Waybill for air freight, or equivalent transport document
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list for exported goods
Foreign Exchange Inward Remittance Certificate or bank-confirmed foreign currency receipt record evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Signed contract or purchase order with the overseas customer
Proof of non-resident status and overseas consumption for zero-rated services or digital products
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service coordinate to verify export declarations, transport documents, and foreign currency receipts. If an export zero-rating claim is not fully substantiated with the required documentation, the supply is reclassified as taxable and 10% VAT is assessed on the gross supply value, with additional tax imposed under the VAT Act and Framework Act on National Taxes for underreporting or non-reporting. Frail, false, or fraudulent zero-rating claims are subject to retrospective assessment over the statutory 10-year limitation period for tax evasion, interest, additional tax of up to 40% or more depending on the degree of fraud, and criminal penalties including fines and imprisonment under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. In addition, false or forged export documents and electronic tax invoices trigger severe statutory penalties and can result in suspension of exporter privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), with Ministry of Economy and Finance exercising Foreign Exchange Transactions Act policy oversight and Korea Customs Service handling trade-related reporting
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized but supervised foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Current account transactions, including export of assembled RPG dice, import of raw materials, service fees, royalties, and ordinary trade payments, are free to execute through authorized foreign exchange banks and require only reporting or post-event verification. Capital account transactions remain subject to a notification, declaration, or approval regime managed by the Bank of Korea and the Ministry of Economy and Finance; inbound foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, overseas borrowing, securities investment, and external guarantees must be filed before settlement. The Korean won is fully convertible for legitimate current account purposes onshore, but the authorities can impose temporary requirements, such as surrender or conversion restrictions, in a balance-of-payments or financial crisis. Profit remittance by a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa is permitted yearly or upon dissolution after audited financial statements are approved; the bank verifies corporate authorization, tax clearance, and the underlying foreign investment registration. A non-resident shareholder's dividend or liquidation proceeds may be converted and sent abroad through the domestic bank using purpose code for overseas remittance. There is no fixed percentage surrender requirement for export receipts, but the exporter must repatriate and report the full export value onshore.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, an exporter must receive export proceeds within six months from the date of export clearance unless an extension is granted by the competent authority. The statutory repatriation obligation is 100% of the invoiced export value; proceeds must be received through a domestic authorized foreign exchange bank. There is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio forcing all foreign currency receipts into Korean won; the exporter may hold the funds in a registered foreign currency account or sell them to the bank at the prevailing market rate. The bank reports receipt through the Korea Customs Service and the Bank of Korea's electronic foreign exchange reporting system, and any unrepatriated or overdue balance must be justified with supporting evidence or face administrative penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low; offshore fintech EMIs are not legally viable as primary treasury banks for a Korean entity. Korean law requires foreign exchange business to be conducted by licensed foreign exchange banks or registered non-bank foreign exchange businesses. Offshored digital EMIs cannot provide Korean won settlement accounts, BOK-Wire+ clearing access, statutory foreign exchange declarations, or inward direct investment registration. Stripe and PayPal may serve only as merchant payment gateways for customer card payments, not as treasury or cross-border settlement rails. The entity must onboard with a tier-1 domestic commercial bank for all regulated currency and liquidity transactions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Yuhan Hoesa with non-resident directors, in-branch identity verification is effectively mandatory at initial onboarding. The statutory representative or authorized signatory must appear personally with original passport, corporate registration certificate, articles of incorporation, and board resolution appointing the signatory. If physical attendance is impossible, a locally resident representative may be appointed under a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, but the bank may still require a video KYC interview with the beneficial owner. Remote consular proxy opening is not automatically accepted by all tier-1 Korean banks; each bank's FATF-compliant onboarding policy applies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholders hold the Korean LLC indirectly through multiple non-resident holding layers, making the UBO and source of funds difficult to identify during initial review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete corporate ownership chain certified by apostille, certified English translations of each entity's registry extract, passports of every UBO above 10%, board resolutions authorizing the LLC opening, and 12 months of personal and business bank statements evidencing lawful source of capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crowdfunding revenue from Kickstarter and Stripe arrives as hundreds of low-value international online payments from pre-sale backers, which may be considered unusual transaction volume or potential money mule layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kickstarter campaign terms, list of backer pledge entries, Stripe settlement records and merchant verification, refund and chargeback policy with execution logs, order fulfilment tracking numbers, and a CPA-prepared sales reconciliation mapping pledges to shipped polyhedral dice sets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border trade involving shipping to jurisdictions with enhanced sanctions and enforcement risk triggers sanctions screening and dual-use due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Korea Customs Service export declarations, HS and ECCN classification certificate confirming the epoxy resin dice are not controlled technology, commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading or airway bills, end-user certificate, and comprehensive OFAC, UN, EU, and Korean sanctions screening reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Minimum capital is legally zero, but a foreign investor's inbound wire for working capital lacks a filed foreign investment notice under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign investment notification and registration certificate issued or received by the Bank of Korea and the Ministry of Economy and Finance, declaration of expected capital, bank certificate of receipt of foreign currency, CPA capital verification report, and a notarized shareholder resolution authorizing the capital injection.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or loan proceeds must be routed as a SWIFT wire to the LLC's Capital Escrow Account or a similar foreign currency account opened under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The wire must originate from the investor's own account and carry the applicable foreign exchange purpose code for inward direct investment. Prior to settlement, the foreign investor must file a foreign investment notification; after receipt, the bank issues a foreign currency acquisition certificate and the remittance is declared against the capital account. If paid-in capital is required for any counterparty or licensing purpose, a Korean certified public accountant prepares a capital verification report before the funds are transferred into the LLC's basic operational account for ongoing treasury use.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements to overseas suppliers and freight agents must be executed through an authorized foreign exchange bank using SWIFT MT103 for open-account payments, irrevocable commercial letters of credit for high-value settlements, and documentary collections such as D/P or D/A when no bank payment undertaking is needed. The Korean bank routes USD through its correspondent clearing network; Korean won cannot be cleared overseas. Each payment must be supported by import declaration, commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or airway bill, and the correct foreign exchange purpose code, with the bank submitting the transaction to the Bank of Korea's reporting system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forwards with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank, limited to the volume and maturity of the underlying import and export contracts.
Non-deliverable forwards (KRW NDFs) for non-resident hedging of offshore won exposure where the underlying trade or loan exposure is documented; onshore speculative NDF positions are not permitted.

Plain-vanilla cross-currency swaps and FX options booked with a domestic bank, used solely to hedge actual cash flows from foreign capital injections, trade receivables, or payables, with all contracts reported to the Bank of Korea and counterparties sanctions-screened.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year fiscal year ending December 31: file and pay by March 31 of the following year; electronic filing carries an automatic administrative extension to April 30, and a further approved audit-related extension may apply to May 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing additional tax equal to 20% of unpaid corporate tax; under-reporting additional tax equal to 10% of understated tax; daily late-payment interest of 0.025% from the statutory due date; prolonged delinquency triggers NTS asset seizure, garnishment, business registration cancellation, and possible court strike-off of an inactive entity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (Si, Gun, Gu) via local tax e-filing portal or integrated NTS filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the national corporate tax filing: March 31 following the December 31 fiscal year end, with electronic filing extension to April 30 where allowed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local Tax Act late-payment surcharge of 3% within the first month and 1.2% per month thereafter (capped at 60% of unpaid tax); coercive collection measures, seizure and compulsory sale of corporate assets, and suspension or cancellation of business registration for non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Preliminary Return for January 1 to June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File and pay on or before July 25 of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing additional tax of 20% of unpaid VAT; under-reporting additional tax of 10%; tax-invoice violations attract additional tax of 2% of supply value; daily late-payment interest of 0.025% and continued delinquency may lead to estimated assessment and cancellation of business registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Final Return for July 1 to December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File and pay on or before January 25 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing additional tax of 20% of unpaid VAT; under-reporting additional tax of 10%; daily late-payment interest of 0.025%; persistent non-compliance triggers asset seizure and administrative closure of the business registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholding Tax Report and Wage and Salary Payment Summary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service via HomeTax regional tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 10 of the year following the payment calendar year for employee and director compensation; monthly withholding remittances remain due by the 10th of each following month throughout the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual withholding report attracts additional tax of 10% of the withheld amount; failure to withhold or remit monthly withholding tax results in collection of unpaid tax plus daily late-payment interest and additional non-withholding penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements Filing (if mandatory audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via DART and National Tax Service with the corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting of members/shareholders approving financial statements must be held by March 31; external audit report must be filed with FSS within 14 days after the meeting; audited financial statements must accompany the corporate tax return by March 31, subject to approved audit-related extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Act on External Audit of Corporations, failure to appoint or file an external auditor exposes the company to fines up to KRW 50,000,000 (approximately USD 37,000), FSS corrective orders, designated auditor appointment, public sanction disclosure, and rejection of unaudited financial statements by NTS

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent certified CPA audit applies to a Korean Yuhan Hoesa whose total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 8.9 million at KRW 1,350/USD); listed companies and companies designated by the Financial Services Commission are also subject to compulsory audit regardless of size. South Korea prescribes no turnover or headcount statutory audit trigger; the controlling quantitative threshold is the total-asset balance sheet test, with additional consolidated and high-public-interest triggers for listed and financial entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed and designated preparers; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) for non-listed companies including private Yuhan Hoesa entities below the audit threshold; audits are performed under Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA), which are converged with International Standards on Auditing (ISA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO return is required for an ordinary non-listed Korean Yuhan Hoesa. Ownership is tracked through the statutory register of members, and any transfer of holdings must be approved in accordance with the articles of incorporation and recorded without undue delay. If a non-resident holds shares in a registered foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a foreign investment notification or change report must be filed through a designated foreign exchange bank or KOTRA within 30 days of acquisition, transfer, capital increase, or change of ownership percentage. Financial institutions and designated AML entities have separate beneficial-owner verification and periodic confirmation duties under Korean anti-money laundering legislation, but a standard low-risk Yuhan Hoesa has no separate government UBO annual filing.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 12,000 for a small manufacturing Yuhan Hoesa; larger mandatory audit engagements may exceed USD 25,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal national corporate income tax rate (tax base over KRW 300 billion); lower bands: 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% for KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21% for KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; plus 10% local income tax surtax on the national corporate tax, producing effective top combined rate of 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No specific patent box or free-zone holiday for ordinary Yuhan Hoesa; available incentives include the R&D tax credit, facility/investment tax credits, SME tax reduction, and foreign-investment tax exemption/reduction in Korean Free Economic Zones/FEZ if the taxpayer obtains foreign investment approval and meets qualification requirements; polyhedral dice casting generally does not qualify for the special high-tech FEZ holiday unless certified by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return (CIT main form) with attached schedules, filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax system at hometax.go.kr; foreign ownership schedule must be attached because the Yuhan Hoesa is 100% eligible for non-resident ownership.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return, complemented by a semi-annual interim tax return/payment that must be filed within two months from the end of the first six months of the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return must be filed within three months from the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the fixed deadline is March 31 of the following year, automatically extended to the next business day if the date falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate legal name, business registration number, and registered address of Yuhan Hoesa, including representative director data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the exact Korean-registered legal name and the 10-digit Korean business registration number. If a non-resident individual is the representative director, complete the supplementary director schedule with passport number and foreign tax identification number; the Korean resident status of the company is determined by place of effective management/incorporation, not by the nationality of the shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates and the tax office jurisdiction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the actual business year. For a newly incorporated or liquidated Yuhan Hoesa, use a short fiscal period. All foreign currency sales from Stripe/PayPal/Kickstarter must be translated into Korean won using the Bank of Korea base exchange rate prevailing on the transaction or year-end date; no permanent establishment disconnection is available because the LLC is a Korean tax resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales, ordinary business income, and non-business income components.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report total worldwide revenue from tabletop polyhedral dice sales, Kickstarter pre-order deposits that have accelerated, Stripe settlement proceeds, PayPal receipts, and any licensing of the dice mold designs. Non-resident shareholders do not themselves file this return; the LLC must file as a Korean domestic corporation. Any intercompany sales to a foreign affiliate must be reported at arm's length and the transaction summary appended.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions, cost of goods sold, operating expenses, depreciation, and other adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only actual, documented expenses incurred in producing the epoxy-resin dice: resin, molds, pigment, packaging, shipping, platform commissions, payment processing fees, studio rent, and wages. Disallow payments to related foreign parties unless supported by contractual evidence and comparable pricing; entertainment, donations, and non-statutory reserves are not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income calculation and progressive corporate tax computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 9%/19%/21%/24% brackets on the taxable base, subtract allowable loss carryforwards (up to ten years), and compute the national corporate income tax. Then compute the 10% local income tax surtax. If the business remains under KRW 200 million of annual taxable income, the effective current burden is 9.9% including local surtax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, withholding tax credit, and taxes paid abroad.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit only foreign income taxes actually paid on Korean-source income or on foreign permanent establishment income, subject to Article 69 of the Corporate Tax Act. Non-resident dividend withholding on distributions to foreign shareholders is not creditable here; it is a tax borne by the shareholder and should not be claimed as a corporate expense or credit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or incomplete filing triggers additional tax under the Corporate Tax Act: 20% penalty on the unpaid tax for a non-filer, 10% to 20% for understatement depending on intentionality, and a 40% penalty for omission/understatement carrying taxable income under unlawful fraudulent schedules. Unpaid or under-withheld amounts attract statutory interest at the national tax default rate. Habitual or fraudulent returns shift the matter to the Tax Evasion Punishment Act, with criminal prosecution and personal criminal liability for the signing director.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax on outbound dividends paid to foreign shareholders, plus 2% local income tax surtax, making the aggregate statutory rate 22%; treaty rate may reduce the aggregate rate if a complete DTA relief file is lodged.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke Bilateral Double Taxation Treaty relief, the foreign shareholder must (i) obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate from the treaty jurisdiction; (ii) complete the NTS Application for Non-Resident Tax Exemption or Reduced Rate before the payment date or, if not applied in time, file a refund claim within the statutory claim period; (iii) provide a beneficial ownership certificate showing the shareholder is the ultimate recipient and has no contractual or de facto obligation to pass the income to a third country resident; (iv) attach the Korean payer's withholding tax return and supporting payment evidence; and (v) maintain substance documentation in case the NTS challenges the beneficial ownership or treaty shopping arrangement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory domestic rates: royalties and interest paid to foreign parties are each subject to 20% national withholding plus 2% local income tax, totaling 22% unless reduced. Applicable DTA rates commonly reduce interest and royalty withholding to 10% or 15%, and dividends to 10% or 15% depending on shareholding threshold; the reduced rate is not automatic and requires the same treaty relief procedure, TRC, and beneficial ownership proof.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: International transaction report required for aggregate foreign related-party transactions of KRW 500 million or more; Local File required when the Korean entity's foreign related-party transactions reach KRW 5 billion in a fiscal year; Master File and CbC reporting generally apply when consolidated group revenue reaches KRW 1 trillion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not use a separately labeled Economic Substance Regulation in the UAE sense, but the substance-over-form doctrine, beneficial ownership gatekeeping, controlled foreign company rules, and tax treaty anti-abuse provisions require the Yuhan Hoesa to carry on real Core Income-Generating Activities in Korea. A foreign-owned LLC must show a Korean office, employees, inventory control, order processing, and management decisions in Korea; if the Korean entity merely routes dice royalties or pre-orders to a shell shareholder, tax authorities may disregard the entity under the piercing-of-veil doctrine and allocate income to the real owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion by Fraudulent Underreporting of Digital Sales
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC omits Stripe, PayPal, and Kickstarter gross receipts, understates polyhedral dice shipment income, or fabricates nonexistent epoxy resin supplier invoices in order to keep taxable income inside the 9% bracket.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 47-2 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and Article 76 of the Corporate Tax Act: 40% unfaithful-return penalty on the evaded tax plus overdue interest. Tax Evasion Punishment Act Article 3 adds criminal liability: imprisonment for up to five years or a fine of up to five times the tax evaded; both penalties can be imposed cumulatively.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Commercial Act Article 401 makes the responsible director personally liable for damages to the company and third parties caused by intentional or negligent breach of duty. The NTS may pierce the corporate veil, hold the director jointly liable, impose a departure-restriction/blacklist order, and the signing director faces criminal imprisonment if the fraudulent return was signed with knowledge.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Yuhan Hoesa pays dividends, interest, or royalties to its non-resident shareholders or related foreign licensors without withholding the 22% aggregate Korean tax, or without obtaining the DTA protective certificates, and then characterizes the payment as a non-taxable offshore transfer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding obligations arise under the Corporate Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes; failure to withhold makes the company and its responsible officers jointly liable for the uncollected tax plus penalties. Additional-penalty tax can reach 100% of the evaded withholding tax when the omission is intentional; the Tax Evasion Punishment Act criminal provisions additionally apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who instruct the treasury to make untaxed outbound distributions become personally liable for the withheld-but-not-remitted tax; the NTS can seize personal bank accounts and real estate, issue a departure-restriction/blacklist order for unpaid withholding debts exceeding the statutory threshold, and recommend criminal prosecution for individual directors, with imprisonment exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Sham and Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC enters into related-party contracts with a shell supplier or intellectual property owner, reports excessive royalty or management fees to the related counterparty, and fails to prepare the International Transaction Report, Local File, or Master File despite exceeding the KRW thresholds, producing a shifted profit base in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 5 and Article 9 of the Framework Act on International Taxation permit the NTS to adjust Korean taxable income to the arm's length price and impose penalties for filing failures; a misreporting penalty of 20% to 40% under the Framework Act on National Taxes, fines for failure to submit TP documentation, and interest are all assessable. If the structure is a sham, substance-over-form and anti-abuse rules recharacterize the supposed non-resident owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face joint secondary liability if the corporation is unable to pay the adjusted tax because they intentionally stripped assets; the doctrine of piercing the corporate veil permits the NTS to attribute the unpaid tax to the controlling individual. The director can also be criminally prosecuted as a conspirator in tax evasion and blacklisted from foreign travel while tax delinquencies remain unpaid.
